description: BCHSI Special Invited Seminar Topic: "Artificial Intelligence for Clinical Decision Making Across Modalities" Lunch Served 12:30 – 1:00 pm Seminar 1:10 – 2:00 pm Rock Hall Auditorium & by Zoom In place of the monthly BCHSI-wide Lab meeting, we will host Dr. Dvir Aran, who is currently a Visiting Scholar at UCSF - join us in welcoming him! FEATURED SPEAKER Dvir Aran, PhD, Associate Professor Faculty of Biology\Taub Faculty of Computer Science Technion -Israel Institute of Technology In this seminar, Dr. Aran will present two recent works that illustrate how artificial intelligence can democratize clinical decision-making. The first develops a deep learning model that predicts breast cancer recurrence risk directly from histopathology images, offering a scalable alternative to costly molecular assays. The second introduces a conversational, multi-agent AI system for neurological diagnosis, which achieves higher accuracy than physicians while reducing costs. Together, these studies show how AI can extend expert-level decision support to settings with limited resources, advancing both equity and efficiency in clinical care. description: “Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder” Presented by: Jasmine Wilaisakditipakorn, MD Clinical Assistant Professor, Department of Pediatrics, Child Development Division UC Davis Health Planners expect learners to: 1. Recognize the clinical features of fetal alcohol spectrum disorders (FASD), including the range of neurodevelopmental, behavioral, and physical manifestations, and understand that many affected individuals do not have characteristic facial features. 2. Apply evidence-based approaches to screening for prenatal alcohol exposure, evaluating children with suspected FASD, and identifying appropriate diagnostic and referral pathways. 3. Develop individualized, multidisciplinary management plans for children with FASD that incorporate medical care, behavioral and developmental interventions, educational supports, and family-centered resources. description: Established through REDS-III and continued through REDS-IV-P, the Brazil SCD cohort is a prospective, longitudinal study designed to generate real-world evidence on the health and clinical outcomes of people living with SCD in Brazil, with a particular focus on transfusion practices and their impact on patient outcomes. This seminar series will feature investigators and clinicians from the REDS Brazil collaboration presenting key findings from the cohort and ongoing work aimed at advancing our understanding of SCD and improving transfusion practices and patient care. September 15, 2026, Shannon Kelly, MD, UCSF Benioff Children’s Hospital Oakland. “Overview of SCD cohort and the main findings”September 22, 2026, Mina Cintho Ozahata, PhD, University of São Paulo. “Phenotype/genotype association studies using the Brazil SCD cohort”September 29, 2026, Brian Custer, PhD, MPH, Vitalant Research Institute. “Development of the precision transfusion medicine array and its use in RBC-IMPACT”October 6, 2026, Carla Dinardo, MD, PhD, and Monike Oliveria, MSc, Fundação Pro-Sangue, São Paulo. “RHD sequencing, alloimmunization & matching studies”We hope you join this exciting series and take the opportunity to learn from our REDS Brazil collaborators and engage in discussion around the future of SCD research.

description: 8-Week Mindfulness-Based Cancer Recovery Program Online Zoom program, with Valeria Galetto, PhD If you have received a cancer diagnosis, you know the emotional part can take a toll on you. Research shows that if you learn how to manage your stress and anxiety, you can improve your quality of life and become an active participant in your own recovery and survivorship. This program is based on Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR), a therapeutic combination of mindfulness meditation, gentle yoga, and simple practices designed to let go of fears and concerns and focus on getting well. Please plan to attend all nine sessions (Including the Saturday Session). The mindfulness subject matter builds from one session to the next, so it is important that attendees can commit to at least 6 of the 8 class sessions to participate. Should these dates not be convenient, please reach out for alternative support at 415-885-3693. description: Session Overview This hands-on workshop focuses on how to best start basic literature searching using a combination of databases, search engines, and AI tools. Discussion will cover questions to consider that guide whether an AI tool, such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Consensus, and Perplexity, can be helpful in the literature searching process. Participants will practice searching a combination of databases, search engines, and AI tools to critique the results. There will be time for questions and discussion throughout the workshop. Learning Objectives Determine where AI tools may fit into the literature searching workflowCompare and contrast answers provided by databases vs. AI toolsCreate prompts to optimize AI tool answers to compliment database searchingRegister to receive the Zoom link and password. About the series This session is part of the AI in your Toolkit: Critical approaches to using AI in your work workshop series. The next workshop is October 8, at 11 a.m. - 12:30 p.m. and covers AI Tools for Review Projects. About the instructor Josephine Tan, MLIS, is an Education and Research Librarian.
